newsitem.title: UK: U.S. investment bank DLJ buys Britain's Phoenix.
newsitem.headline: U.S. investment bank DLJ buys Britain's Phoenix.

text.p: U.S. investment bank Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette said on Tuesday it would buy British financial advisory firm Phoenix Group Ltd.
The new group, called DLJ Phoenix, would play a leading role in developing DLJ's investment banking business in Europe and Asia, the firms said in a joint statement.
The companies said Martin Smith, a founding partner of Phoenix, would serve as chairman of DLJ Phoenix and all of Phoenix's 25 directors and staff would be retained.
DLJ, based in New York, employs 5,900 people worldwide and describes itself as the leading distributor of U.S. equity securities to institutional investors outside the United States.
Britain's Sunday Telegraph reported two days ago the deal would be worth around 50 million pounds ($80 million) but DLJ chairman and chief executive John Chalsty declined to comment.
"We're not going to talk about that...we don't know where that number came from," Chalsty said in a telephone interview.

Chalsty said DLJ believed Phoenix could offer expertise in mergers and acquisitions and could help the group develop high-yield business and target newly emerging companies in eastern Europe and Russia.

Chalsty said DLJ had been present in London for 20 years but had focused on selling U.S equities to European institutions. He said DLJ was not looking for further acquisitions in London. ($1=.6199 Pound)
